faq.q: Which is faster, the Pershing 46 or the Sunseeker Predator 55?
faq.a: The Pershing 46 typically reaches around 40 knots, while the Sunseeker Predator 55 cruises at about 35 knots. The Pershing is lighter and more agile, making it the better choice for speed lovers. However, the Predator offers a smoother ride at high speed thanks to its larger hull.

faq.q: How many passengers can each boat accommodate?
faq.a: The Pershing 46 carries up to 10 passengers plus skipper. The Sunseeker Predator 55 holds up to 12 passengers. For larger groups, the Predator has more deck space and a larger cockpit, but the Pershing feels more intimate and sporty.

faq.q: What is the charter price for the Pershing 46 in Marbella?

faq.q: Is the Sunseeker Predator 55 available for charter in Marbella?

faq.q: Which boat is better for a day trip to Cabopino or Estepona?
faq.a: Both are excellent. The Pershing 46 is more nimble and fun for shorter trips to Cala del Faro or Cabopino. The Predator 55 offers more comfort for longer cruises to Estepona or Sotogrande. If you want to anchor and swim, the Predator’s larger platform is better.

faq.q: What amenities are included on the Pershing 46 charter?
faq.a: Every Pershing 46 charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). You can also bring your own food and music. The boat has a sun pad, wet bar, and cabin for changing.

faq.q: Can I charter the Pershing 46 for a sunset cruise from Puerto Banús?
faq.a: Absolutely. The Pershing 46 is a popular choice for sunset cruises. Departing from Puerto Banús, you can cruise along the Marbella coastline, watch the sunset over La Concha, and anchor near the Golden Mile. Minimum booking is 2 hours (€749 for Tier A boats, but Pershing is pricing on request).

faq.q: Which boat is more luxurious, the Pershing 46 or the Sunseeker Predator 55?
faq.a: Both are high-end. The Predator 55 has more interior space, a larger saloon, and a more opulent finish. The Pershing 46 is sportier and more minimalist, with a focus on performance. If luxury means space and comfort, go Predator; if luxury means speed and style, go Pershing.

data.body_html:
When you’re planning a luxury boat charter in Marbella, two names often come up: the Pershing 46 and the Sunseeker Predator 55. Both are sleek, powerful, and turn heads in Puerto Banús. But which one should you choose for your day on the Costa del Sol? In this showdown, we compare speed, space, price, and the overall charter experience — with a focus on the Pershing 46, which is available in our fleet.

Pershing 46 vs Sunseeker Predator 55: Specs at a Glance

FeaturePershing 46Sunseeker Predator 55
Length14m17.5m
Passengers1012
Top Speed~40 knots~35 knots
DeparturePuerto BanúsPuerto Banús (not in our fleet)
Charter PriceOn requestTypically €2,500–€4,000/day

The Pershing 46 is a pure sport cruiser: lightweight, agile, and built for speed. The Sunseeker Predator 55 is larger, with more deck space and a flybridge option — but it’s also heavier and pricier. For a pure adrenaline rush, the Pershing wins. For lounging and entertaining a bigger group, the Predator has the edge.

Performance: Which Boat Is Faster?

The Pershing 46 hits around 40 knots with its twin MAN diesels (about 800 hp each). The Predator 55, with twin Volvo Penta IPS 900s, cruises at 30–35 knots. On the water, the Pershing feels like a sports car — it planes quickly, handles tight turns, and responds instantly. The Predator is more of a grand tourer: stable, smooth, but less thrilling. If you want to feel the wind in your hair and race along the Marbella coast to Cala Cortés, the Pershing is your boat.

Space and Comfort: Which Is Better for a Group?

The Pershing 46 seats 10 guests comfortably. Its open layout includes a large sun pad aft, a C-shaped sofa in the cockpit, and a small cabin for changing. The Predator 55 offers more room: a larger cockpit, a separate sun deck, and a more spacious saloon. For a day trip with 10–12 friends, the Predator gives everyone more personal space. But the Pershing’s compact design creates a more social, party-like atmosphere — perfect for a group of 8–10 who want to stay close.

Charter Cost: Pershing 46 vs Predator 55 in Marbella

The Pershing 46 is available in our fleet — pricing is on request via WhatsApp. Typically, a half-day (4 hours) starts around €1,500–€2,000, and a full day (8 hours) around €2,500–€3,500. The Sunseeker Predator 55, if chartered through other operators, usually costs 30–50% more due to its size and luxury finish. Both include skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and VAT. For a high-speed experience without the premium price tag, the Pershing 46 offers better value.

Which Boat Should You Charter in Marbella?

Choose the Pershing 46 if you want:

  • Adrenaline and speed (40 knots)
  • A sporty, intimate vibe for up to 10 guests
  • Lower charter cost compared to larger yachts
  • A quick getaway from Puerto Banús to Cabopino or Estepona

Choose the Sunseeker Predator 55 if you want:

  • More deck space and a flybridge
  • Accommodation for up to 12 guests
  • A more luxurious, laid-back cruising experience
  • To impress with sheer size and presence

Since the Predator 55 isn’t in our fleet, we recommend the Pershing 46 as a direct alternative. For even more space, consider our Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax, from €4,719 for 4 hours including a jet ski).

Where Can You Go on a Pershing 46 Charter?

Departing from Puerto Banús, you can cruise north to Cabopino (20 minutes) or south to Estepona (30 minutes). For a longer trip, head to Sotogrande (1 hour). Popular anchorages include Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés, where you can swim, snorkel, and enjoy the Mediterranean. The Pershing’s shallow draft (1.2m) lets you get close to the shore. Don’t forget to stop for a photo with La Concha mountain in the background.

What’s Included on a Pershing 46 Charter?

Every charter includes:

  • Licensed skipper
  • Fuel
  • Water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava
  • Light snacks
  • Insurance and safety equipment
  • Spanish IVA (21%)

You can also bring your own food and drinks. The boat has a small cabin with a toilet and a shower — handy for changing after a swim.
